sector_model: Large pharma and medtech: adjusted vs GAAP earnings, FCF after SBC, litigation liability, net debt
thesis: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), Innovative Medicine (Q3 sales 16,757M, +7.7%) and MedTech (8,642M, +2.5%). Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-27; 10-Q 0000200406-26-000197 filed 2026-10-21, release 2026-10-13): sales 25,399M (+5.9%), GAAP net earnings only 210M (EPS 0.09) vs 5,152M because of a one-time special charge for the proposed ovarian talc resolution plus Firefly Bio and Sail Biomedicines deals (dollar amounts not stated in the release text I read; secondary summaries differ at 5.5B to about 7B, unverified; GAAP to adjusted gap 6,129M vs about 1,650M a year earlier implies roughly 4.5B above normal adjustments). Adjusted EPS 2.59 (-7.5%). 2026 guide raised: reported sales 101.0-101.4B, adjusted EPS 11.05-11.15 (midpoint 11.10, +2.9%). TTM (4Q ended 2026-09-27) sales 99,335M, GAAP net earnings 16,095M, OCF 26,159M, capex 5,569M, FCF 20,590M, SBC 1,424M, so FCF after SBC 19,166M. At 285.75 (2026-11-13 close, 52-week 193.45 to 288.11, near the high) and 2.41B shares (stockanalysis; cover count unread), market cap about 688B: 42.8x TTM GAAP, 25.7x adjusted guide midpoint, FCF yield 3.0% (2.8% after SBC), dividend 5.36 = 1.9%. 9M buybacks 5,958M. Cash and equivalents 16,910M, noncurrent debt 35,799M (current debt and marketable securities not read), so net debt at least about 19B before current debt. Market view: the stock rerated about 48% off its 52-week low as pharma growth and a talc resolution lower tail risk; at 25.7x adjusted for about 3% EPS growth the price already assumes durable pipeline replacement of Stelara erosion. The business is high quality; the price is not obviously cheap.
counterthesis: The talc charge is large and unquantified in what I read; a proposed resolution is not final and cash payments will reduce FCF over time. GAAP earnings are dominated by special items; TTM GAAP 42.8x is a poor valuation basis and adjusted EPS excludes recurring acquisition and litigation costs. Adjusted EPS fell 7.5% in Q3 and guidance implies only +2.9% for 2026, while the stock is at 25.7x adjusted, near its 52-week high. MedTech growth is only +2.5% and international +1.5%. Stelara biosimilar erosion, tariffs, drug price negotiation and Medicare pricing, and the Intra-Cellular acquisition integration are unreviewed. Peers (LLY, ABBV, MRK, PFE, ABT) not compared; JNJ is a large holding in broad US index funds, so it duplicates index exposure.
invalidation: Thesis fails if the talc resolution cost rises well above the charge or collapses into new litigation, 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is cut, Innovative Medicine growth drops below about 4%, or the multiple expands further without earnings growth.
